narrative.overview:
The website is a flight console looking out on the Solar System of 2250. It is a dark, sober instrument panel: a fixed star-field photograph under a 40% black veil, and on top of it content held in teal hologram frames. Everything is lit from within, with thin luminous lines and no soft fills. The setting is hard science (physics, water, metals, the speed of light), so the interface reads as equipment, not fantasy. Decoration is limited to frames, rules and corner brackets, as if drawn by light.

Edges are never plain right angles. Frames are chamfered, with diagonal cut corners and lines that look like coloured light beams. Text and images always sit inside such a frame or behind a rule. State is signalled by a shift from teal to red: the idle signal is teal, and hover, selection and active states warm to red.

Typography is German-language and pairs a Latin Modern Sans reading face with Latin Modern Mono Caps for every title, label and navigation item, which gives a technical-manual voice. Density is moderate on lore pages and dense on deck and trade screens so card data stays exact and legible.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only: black void, teal signal, red alert. There is no light theme.
Chamfered hologram frames (image-based) around every content block.
Teal means idle and information, red means interaction and state change.
Mono-caps titles, sans body text, with no other typefaces.
Flat: depth comes from glow, translucency and layering, never from drop shadows.

rules.name: The Teal-to-Red Rule
rules.body: Idle is teal and interaction is red. A hover or selected state shifts a teal element to red (or a red-tinted glow); it never introduces a third hue. Red at rest is reserved for warnings and errors.

rules.name: The Pale-for-Small-Text Rule
rules.body: Signal Teal Bright and Alert Red do not carry small text on black at WCAG AA. Body-size text on the dark background is white, Signal Teal Pale, Alert Red Pale or Alert Red Bright. Saturated teal and red are for lines, fills, large labels and icons.

rules.name: The Veil Rule
rules.body: The star photograph is always under the 40% black veil. Never place content straight on the unveiled sky.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Titles, labels and navigation are Mono Caps, and everything that is read as a sentence is Sans. Never set a paragraph in Mono Caps or a title in Sans.

rules.name: The No-Third-Font Rule
rules.body: Only the two Latin Modern faces plus the icon font. The Material default Roboto must not leak in; the global `*` rule forces Latin Modern Sans.

rules.name: The Glow-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is a halo or a line of light, never a cast shadow. Never add `box-shadow` to custom components.

dos: Do shift teal elements to red on hover, focus and selection (Alert Red #991111 fills, Alert Red Pale text), and keep red out of idle surfaces.
Do frame images and text blocks in a content box or with chamfered, beam-like lines; follow the zone-corner and frame art for any new shape.
Do set titles, labels and navigation in Latin Modern Mono Caps and prose in Latin Modern Sans at 18px, line-height 1.7, capped at 75ch.
Do use Signal Teal Pale (#88cccc) or white for small text on black, and keep WCAG AA contrast.
Do keep the 40% black veil under all content and keep the page flat (halo and translucent tint, no shadows).
Do show a placeholder (the star field) when card or lore images are missing, and keep page structure intact.
Do give every interactive element a visible focus state. This is the product's accessibility default.
donts: Don't use plain rounded rectangles, pills or 90-degree outlined boxes for new components; the language is chamfered, hologram-like.
Don't add drop shadows, gradients as decoration or any light theme.
Don't use saturated teal (#119999) or Alert Red (#991111) as small body text on black.
Don't introduce a third accent hue; teal, red and white on black is the whole palette.
Don't use fantasy or space-opera visuals (nebula clouds, glowing orbs, sci-fi chrome). The setting is hard science with no warp drives, aliens or wonder machines.
Don't set paragraphs in Mono Caps, and don't let Roboto or any default Material font through.
Don't put card or rules content in anything that obscures exact reading of card text; legibility beats effect.
